$comment: How AdCodicem.Pdf compares with other PDF products. Every claim about another product names its source; a value nobody could establish from public sources is 'unknown'. Our own column is derived from docs/features/features.json through each capability's 'ours' features. Regenerate the tables with: ADCODICEM_UPDATE_FEATURE_TABLES=1 dotnet test --project tests/AdCodicem.Pdf.Tests -c Release

products.name: AdCodicem.Pdf
products.pricingModel: Free
products.runtime: Fully managed; no native binary, browser or external process
products.bestAt: Reading and assembling third-party PDFs frugally, then generating business documents from HTML without a browser.

products.name: PDFsharp and MigraDoc
products.pricingModel: Free (MIT); paid support plans, attribution-free license and PsX add-ons on request
products.runtime: Fully managed (Core build); GDI+/WPF builds Windows-only
products.bestAt: Free MIT library for code-built PDFs (drawing API, MigraDoc layout) and for merging, splitting and editing PDFs.

products.name: QuestPDF
products.pricingModel: Free under revenue threshold; else perpetual per-entity license with annual update renewal
products.runtime: Native Skia and qpdf binaries per platform, via P/Invoke
products.bestAt: Code-first fluent C# layout of business documents to PDF, including PDF/A-2/3, PDF/UA-1 and ZUGFeRD invoices.

products.name: PdfPig
products.pricingModel: Free, open source
products.runtime: Fully managed; Skia rendering is a separate native add-on
products.bestAt: Extracting positioned letters and words, with layout analysis and reading order, from existing PDFs in pure C#.

products.name: iText 9
products.pricingModel: Free under AGPL; otherwise an annual subscription by volume, or OEM; some add-ons commercial only
products.runtime: Managed; the OCR add-on is native, rendering an external CLI
products.bestAt: Mature library, strongest at PAdES signing and validation, PDF/A-1 to 4, PDF/UA-1 and 2, and forms; add-ons for HTML, redaction and OCR.

products.name: Aspose.PDF for .NET
products.pricingModel: Perpetual per developer or site with a year of updates; or metered pay-per-use
products.runtime: Managed; System.Drawing.Common, or the .Drawing variant
products.bestAt: Broad commercial SDK: creation, conversion to and from Office formats, forms, signatures, redaction, PDF/A, PDF/UA and ZUGFeRD.

products.name: Syncfusion PDF Library
products.pricingModel: Per developer per year + annual document-volume tier; free Community License
products.runtime: Managed core; bundled Chromium for HTML; native add-ons
products.bestAt: Broad commercial SDK: edit, forms, PAdES B-LTA signing and validation, PDF/A-1 to 4, Factur-X, Blink HTML

products.name: IronPDF
products.pricingModel: Perpetual tiers by devs/locations/projects, 1 yr updates; monthly and enterprise options
products.runtime: Native CEF + PDFium/qpdf binaries, or IronPdfEngine Docker
products.bestAt: Pixel-faithful Chromium HTML/Razor to PDF from .NET, with a broad commercial API for editing, signing, PDF/A and PDF/UA.

products.name: Apryse SDK
products.pricingModel: Custom quote; modular base package plus add-ons, by volume and deployment; free trial
products.runtime: Native PDFNetC core per platform behind a .NET wrapper
products.bestAt: Broad commercial toolkit: rendering, editing, conversion, forms, signatures, PDF/A, redaction and OCR from one native core.

products.name: Nutrient .NET SDK (GdPicture.NET)
products.pricingModel: Annual or multiyear subscription, quoted by component and use case; 30-day trial
products.runtime: Managed .NET plus native runtimes; Chrome for HTML
products.bestAt: Wide .NET document-imaging suite: PDF editing, OCR, barcodes, PDF/A and PDF/UA conversion, signatures and e-invoice embedding.

products.name: Docotic.Pdf
products.pricingModel: Perpetual per app, per server or unbound; unlimited developers; 1 year of updates
products.runtime: Managed .NET; HTML add-on drives headless Chrome
products.bestAt: Managed .NET library for editing, text extraction, forms, signatures and PDF/A, with a free Chrome-based HTML add-on.

products.name: GemBox.Pdf
products.pricingModel: Perpetual per-developer tiers, royalty-free; 1 year of updates; free mode (2 pages)
products.runtime: .NET plus SkiaSharp/HarfBuzz native; Chromium for HTML
products.bestAt: Simple .NET API to read, edit, sign and redact PDFs, with a free two-page mode that may be used commercially.

products.name: Chromium through PuppeteerSharp or Playwright
products.pricingModel: Free, open source
products.runtime: External Chromium process; Playwright adds a Node.js driver
products.bestAt: Browser-grade HTML, CSS and JavaScript to PDF from .NET via headless Chromium; cannot open or modify existing PDFs.

products.name: wkhtmltopdf (DinkToPdf, Rotativa)
products.pricingModel: Free (open source)
products.runtime: Native wkhtmltopdf binary or libwkhtmltox per platform
products.bestAt: Long the default free HTML to PDF command-line tool; now archived, with SSRF flaw CVE-2022-35583 left unpatched.

products.name: Gotenberg
products.pricingModel: Free (open source), sponsor-funded; no paid tier
products.runtime: Docker container (Chromium, LibreOffice) over HTTP
products.bestAt: Self-hosted HTTP API bundling Chromium and LibreOffice for HTML and Office to PDF, plus merge, split, PDF/A and encryption.

products.name: Apache PDFBox
products.pricingModel: Free (open source)
products.runtime: JVM (Java 8+), pure Java
products.bestAt: Mature open-source Java library to read, edit, sign and render PDFs, with Preflight for PDF/A-1b validation.

products.name: qpdf
products.pricingModel: Free (open source)
products.runtime: Native C++ library and CLI (zlib, libjpeg)
products.bestAt: Structural PDF transformation: linearization, encryption, merge and split, repair, and JSON inspection of PDF internals.

products.name: MuPDF and PyMuPDF
products.pricingModel: Free under AGPL; commercial license quoted (OEM per copy, subscription or custom)
products.runtime: Native C library per platform (Python, .NET bindings)
products.bestAt: Fast rendering and text extraction, with a light HTML/CSS layout engine and bindings for Python and .NET.

products.name: pdfcpu
products.pricingModel: Free (open source)
products.runtime: Pure Go (no cgo); Go library or static CLI binary
products.bestAt: Pure-Go PDF processing: validate, merge, split, encrypt, stamp and optimize, as a library or a static CLI.

products.name: WeasyPrint
products.pricingModel: Free (open source); optional paid professional support
products.runtime: CPython 3.10+ with native Pango, HarfBuzz, Fontconfig
products.bestAt: Browser-free HTML/CSS paged-media to PDF engine in Python, with PDF/A and PDF/UA output variants.

products.name: Prince
products.pricingModel: Annual site license by document type/volume; one-time server/desktop; OEM; free non-comm.
products.runtime: Native binary per platform, run as an external process
products.bestAt: High-fidelity CSS paged-media typesetting of HTML and XML, used for books, reports and business documents.

capabilities.name: Managed core: no native binary, browser or external process

itext.note: Core ships as managed DLLs (io, kernel, layout, forms, pdfa, pdfua, sign, svg, barcodes, styledxmlparser), and pdfHTML is also managed. The exceptions are pdfOCR, which needs native OCR runtimes, and pdfRender, which is an external CLI

aspose.note: Managed assemblies only (no native runtimes in the NuGet packages), no browser or external process. On non-Windows .NET 8+ use the Aspose.PDF.Drawing variant, because the main package relies on System.Drawing.Common. Optional OCR brings in Aspose.OCR, which uses native ONNX Runtime

syncfusion.note: Core package is managed; HTML needs bundled Blink; raster (PDFium), OCR (Tesseract), Imaging (SkiaSharp) are native

pdfsharp.note: Core build is pure managed C# (net8/9/10, netstandard2.0); GDI+ and WPF builds are Windows-only

questpdf.note: P/Invokes bundled native libraries per platform: a custom Skia build (m154) and qpdf (12.4.1).

pdfpig.note: Pure C#, no native code; only the optional Skia rendering add-on is native (filter add-ons are managed).

ironpdf.note: Needs native packages (IronPdf.Native.Chrome.*, IronSoftware.Native.PdfModel) or the remote IronPdfEngine container

chromium.note: Drives an external Chromium process from downloaded browser binaries; Playwright .NET also runs a Node.js driver

capabilities.oursNote: The core has no dependency at all. The HTML engine (M12) will use SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp, native libraries, for images and text shaping, and the rasterizer (M25) Skia (ADR 43).

capabilities.name: Native AOT, documented

itext.note: The 9.2.0 release notes claim Native AOT support for iText Core, but only in .NET MAUI (iOS/macOS), and 9.3.0 improved MAUI compatibility. The netstandard2.0/net461 assemblies carry no trimming or AOT-compatibility markings. Nothing is documented for server or console Native AOT, or for the add-ons

aspose.note: The system requirements, release notes and docs say nothing about Native AOT or trimming. In a 2023 vendor-forum thread, a user found that PublishTrimmed broke Aspose.PDF 22.12 with a TypeLoadException until trimming was turned off. No vendor statement for Aspose.PDF was found (a 2023 'unsupported' answer was about Aspose.Cells)

syncfusion.note: No Native AOT or trimming statement in docs or release notes; 34.2.9 assembly has no IsAotCompatible metadata

pdfsharp.note: No documented AOT support; 6.2.4 net10.0 PdfSharp.dll declares IsAotCompatible (net8.0 only IsTrimmable)

questpdf.note: 2026.7.0 added full Native AOT and trimming support (IsAotCompatible on net8.0+); native Skia/qpdf still ship.

pdfpig.note: IsAotCompatible on net8.0+, IsTrimmable on net6.0+ (v0.1.10, #939); text exporters need unreferenced code.

ironpdf.note: Vendor's .NET 8 article lists IronPDF as not Native AOT compatible because it embeds the Chromium runtime

chromium.note: PuppeteerSharp states AOT support (PuppeteerSharp.Cdp for Chrome-only); Playwright .NET AOT issue #2714 still open

capabilities.oursNote: The core is written for Native AOT and trimming (invariant 1); verifying it on every corpus document is M23's.

capabilities.name: Opens damaged files by rebuilding the index

itext.note: PdfReader rebuilds the xref when reading it throws (HasRebuiltXref) and fixes object offsets (HasFixedXref). StrictnessLevel controls how lenient it is

aspose.note: Document.Repair(RepairOptions); PdfFileSanitization.RebuildXrefAndTrailer added in 22.8 (PDFNET-50528 'Add method for rebuild xref table')

syncfusion.note: OpenAndRepair overload fixes basic cross-reference offset errors; docs say it cannot repair complex corruption

pdfsharp.note: Tolerates misnumbered xref entries but never rebuilds the xref; a missing startxref or bad offset throws

questpdf.note: Undocumented: DocumentOperation runs qpdf with its default xref recovery; warnings don't throw; no report.

pdfpig.note: Lenient parsing by default; if the xref cannot be read it brute-forces objects and xref sections.

ironpdf.note: No repair API; vendor troubleshooting says IronPDF cannot parse a corrupted PDF

chromium.note: Generates PDFs from web pages only; no API opens or rebuilds existing PDFs

capabilities.oursNote: Every repair is reported as a structured diagnostic.

itext.note: The pdfHTML add-on (itext.pdfhtml) is 'not based on any browser engine implementation'. It can output tagged PDF, PDF/A or PDF/UA

aspose.note: Built-in HTML/CSS engine via HtmlLoadOptions (print/screen media, SVG, font embedding, logical structure via CreateLogicalStructure since 25.12). No Chromium or external process

syncfusion.note: Bundled Blink (Chromium 147) packages; URL, HTML string and SVG input; TOC, bookmarks, forms, headers/footers

pdfsharp.note: FAQ: no HTML-to-PDF converter and none planned; only the third-party HtmlRenderer.PdfSharp

questpdf.note: Code-first C# API only; full HTML/CSS not planned, an HTML subset sits in the backlog; community add-ons only.

pdfpig.note: The wiki lists 'Converting HTML or other document formats to PDF' under things you can't do.

ironpdf.note: Bundled Chromium (CEF 109; CEF 131 in IronPdf.UpdatedChrome): HTML, files, URLs, Razor/CSHTML, JavaScript

chromium.note: page.pdf()/PdfAsync prints the page in headless Chromium (Blink layout, JavaScript executed)

capabilities.name: CSS paged media beyond page size and margins

itext.note: Through pdfHTML: @page rules with margin boxes (e.g. @bottom-right) and counter(page)/counter(pages), running elements (CssRunningManager in the pdfHTML source), and target-counter/target-counters since pdfHTML 3.0.3

aspose.note: CSS @page rules can override PageInfo (HtmlLoadOptions.IsPriorityCssPageRule), so page size and margins can come from CSS. Margin boxes, running headers, page counters, cross-references and footnotes are not documented for Aspose.PDF. break-inside: avoid was unsupported in 2022 (enhancement PDFNET-51824), still unresolved in July 2023

syncfusion.note: Docs cover page size, margins, print media type and API headers/footers; no @page or margin-box support documented

pdfsharp.note: No HTML/CSS engine; MigraDoc does headers, footers, page fields and TOC through its own object model

questpdf.note: No HTML/CSS input; the C# API has repeating headers/footers, page numbers, page references and TOC.

pdfpig.note: No HTML/CSS engine and no layout engine at all.

ironpdf.note: @page size/margins honored; running headers and page numbers via HtmlHeaderFooter API; margin boxes undocumented

chromium.note: @page margin boxes with page/pages counters since Chrome 131; string-set, target-counter, float: footnote unsupported

itext.note: PdfMerger and CopyPagesTo merge documents. PdfSplitter splits by page numbers, size or outlines. PdfDocument.MovePage reorders pages. Tiling and N-up are done through PdfCanvas transforms

aspose.note: Merge, split, move/reorder, insert, delete and extract pages through PageCollection or the PdfFileEditor facade

syncfusion.note: Merge, split, import, reorder, remove and rotate pages

pdfsharp.note: Modify, merge and split existing PDF files: import, insert, move and remove pages

questpdf.note: DocumentOperation (qpdf) MergeFile and TakePages: ranges, any order, reverse, even/odd; split by saving selections.

pdfpig.note: PdfMerger merges files with per-file page selection; AddPage(document, n) copies pages to split or reorder.

ironpdf.note: Merge, AppendPdf/PrependPdf/InsertPdf, CopyPages, RemovePages and split

chromium.note: pageRanges only selects pages of the PDF being generated; no merge/split/reorder of existing PDFs

capabilities.name: Stamps and watermarks on existing pages

itext.note: Text or image watermarks with transparency (PdfExtGState) are added to existing pages through PdfCanvas in stamping mode

aspose.note: TextStamp, ImageStamp and PdfPageStamp via Page.AddStamp on existing pages; WatermarkArtifact; PdfFileStamp facade

syncfusion.note: Text and image watermarks drawn on existing pages, plus watermark annotations

pdfsharp.note: XGraphics.FromPdfPage with Append/Prepend draws text or images on existing pages; vendor Watermark sample

questpdf.note: OverlayFile/UnderlayFile put pages of another PDF over/under chosen pages (watermark example); no direct text call.

pdfpig.note: Can draw text, shapes and JPEG/PNG over copied pages; no stamp API or opacity; README: edits 'very limited'.

ironpdf.note: TextStamper, ImageStamper, HtmlStamper, BarcodeStamper and ApplyWatermark on existing pages

chromium.note: Watermarks only via HTML/CSS or header/footer templates while generating; cannot open existing PDF pages

itext.note: PdfTextExtractor with location-based and simple strategies. The commercial pdfCalligraph add-on advertises extraction for writing systems with compound characters

aspose.note: TextAbsorber, TextFragmentAbsorber and ParagraphAbsorber (paragraph extraction)

syncfusion.note: Plain and layout-preserving extraction; lines, words and glyphs with bounds, font and color

pdfsharp.note: Core gives only raw content-stream characters via CLexer; PsX Text Extractor (separate license) does extraction

questpdf.note: Reading existing PDFs, including text extraction, is only a Future item on the vendor roadmap.

pdfpig.note: Core purpose: positioned letters, word extractors, page segmenters, reading-order detection.

ironpdf.note: ExtractAllText and ExtractTextFromPage(s); images too; JSON export since 2025.12.2

chromium.note: No API reads existing PDFs; headless mode cannot navigate to a PDF document

itext.note: PdfAcroForm fills AcroForm fields and flattens them fully or partially (FlattenFields, PartialFormFlattening). XFDF is supported (XfdfObjectFactory). Core can fill XFA data (XfaForm), but flattening dynamic XFA needs the commercial pdfXFA add-on

aspose.note: Fill AcroForm fields through document.Form; flatten with Field.Flatten, Form.Flatten or Document.Flatten. XFA fields can be filled, or the form converted to AcroForm

syncfusion.note: Create, fill and flatten AcroForm fields; fills XFA through the AcroForm API (EnableXfaFormFill)

pdfsharp.note: Core AcroForm support is limited, with no flatten API; PsX Forms (separate license) creates and manages forms

questpdf.note: Basic AcroForm support (create fields, read values) is only a Future roadmap item; no form operations exist.

pdfpig.note: AcroForm fields are read-only; the wiki lists populating AcroForms under things you can't do (#797).

ironpdf.note: Fill AcroForm text, checkbox, combo and radio fields via Form.FindFormField; flatten with PdfDocument.Flatten

chromium.note: HTML form automation only; no API to fill or flatten AcroForm fields in a PDF

itext.note: Password and certificate encryption through WriterProperties, from RC4 up to AES-256. AES-GCM (ISO/TS 32003) and MAC integrity protection (ISO/TS 32004) since 9.0

aspose.note: Document.Encrypt with CryptoAlgorithm.AESx256 (also RC4-40, RC4-128 and AES-128); public-certificate encryption added in 25.7

syncfusion.note: RC4 40/128, AES 128/256, and AES-GCM 256 (PDF 2.0 only); passwords and permissions

pdfsharp.note: RC4 40/128, AES-128 (default) and AES-256 (PDF 2.0); passwords and permissions

questpdf.note: DocumentOperation.Encrypt with 40-, 128- or 256-bit (AES-256) keys and permission flags; Decrypt too.

pdfpig.note: Only reads encrypted files given a password (RC4/AES); the writer has no encryption.

ironpdf.note: User/owner passwords and permissions; RC4-128 by default, AES-128/AES-256 via EncryptionType since 2026.8.1

chromium.note: Page.printToPDF has no password, permission or encryption parameter

itext.note: PdfPadesSigner covers PAdES B-B, B-T, B-LT and B-LTA, and ProlongSignatures adds LTV data. It needs the BouncyCastle adapter package

aspose.note: Creates PKCS#1, PKCS#7 and PKCS#7-detached signatures with RSA, DSA or ECDSA keys. PKCS#1 and PKCS#7 are always SHA-1; SHA-2 (and SHA-3 for ECDSA) apply only to detached signatures. Also supports external/HSM signing and TSA timestamps. PAdES and ETSI.CAdES.detached are not documented; staff said in February 2022 that Aspose.PDF 'does not meet PADES standards' (PDFNET-42596). A Signature.UseLtv flag exists. A 2024 report of non-compliant PAdES LTV signatures (PDFNET-58018) was answered in January 2025 only by adding SHA-256 for ExternalSignature. B-LT/B-LTA are not documented

syncfusion.note: CAdES/PAdES signatures, timestamps, LTV (DSS) and PAdES B-LTA archive timestamps; external/HSM signing

pdfsharp.note: Since 6.2.0: adbe.pkcs7.detached CMS signatures with optional RFC 3161 timestamp; no PAdES, no DSS/LTV

questpdf.note: X.509 signing is only a Future roadmap item; no PAdES or LTV.

pdfpig.note: No signing; signature fields can only be read, as AcroSignatureField.

ironpdf.note: PFX/X509Certificate2 or HSM (PKCS#11), ECDSA, RFC 3161 timestamps; no documented PAdES baseline or LTV (DSS)

chromium.note: No signing parameter in Page.printToPDF and no PDF manipulation API

capabilities.name: Validation of received signatures

itext.note: SignatureValidator arrived in 8.0.5 as experimental and was finalized in 9.0. It checks integrity, the certificate chain up to trust anchors, OCSP/CRL revocation, timestamps and document revisions (MDP). EU trusted lists (LOTL) arrived in 9.3 and non-EU lists in 9.6

aspose.note: VerifySignature, plus TryVerifySignature (26.7), check integrity and compromise. ValidationOptions add certificate-chain and OCSP/CRL revocation checks (25.1/25.4). No documented LTV/DSS-based long-term validation

syncfusion.note: ValidateSignature: modification, certificate chain, timestamp and OCSP/CRL revocation, custom trusted list

pdfsharp.note: Signature API only signs (IDigitalSigner, DigitalSignatureHandler); no integrity, chain or revocation checks

questpdf.note: Cannot inspect existing PDFs; signing and content inspection are only Future roadmap items.

pdfpig.note: Signature fields are exposed as form fields only; no integrity, certificate or revocation checks.

ironpdf.note: VerifyPdfSignatures: integrity, trust chain, revocation, algorithm strength (2026.3.1); no LTV validation documented

chromium.note: Cannot open existing PDFs; headless mode cannot navigate to a PDF document

capabilities.oursNote: M04, earlier and without cryptography, will report what each signature covers and what changed after it.

itext.note: PDF/A-1a/1b, 2a/2b/2u, 3a/3b/3u, 4, 4e and 4f, through PdfADocument

aspose.note: Converts to PDF/A-1a/1b, 2a/2b/2u, 3a/3b/3u, 4, 4e and 4f

syncfusion.note: Creates PDF/A-1a/b, 2a/b/u, 3a/b/u, 4/4e/4f; ConvertToPDFA converts existing files (Imaging package on .NET Core)

pdfsharp.note: 'Very early state': 6.2.4 SetPdfA writes PDF/A-1a for new tagged documents only; 7.0 preview adds PdfAManager

questpdf.note: PDF/A-2a/2b/2u and 3a/3b/3u; PDF/A-1 is commented out of the enum; no PDF/A-4.

pdfpig.note: ArchiveStandard writes PDF/A-1b, 2b, 3b; the 1a/2a/3a options only add an empty StructTreeRoot.

ironpdf.note: SaveAsPdfA/ConvertToPdfA from HTML or existing PDFs: PDF/A-1a/1b, 2a/2b, 3a/3b, 4/4e/4f (default 3b)

chromium.note: Page.printToPDF offers no PDF/A conformance option

itext.note: Conformance is enforced only on documents written through PdfADocument (created or stamped), which throws PdfAConformanceException on a violation. The vendor says client code is still responsible for full compliance. The docs describe no standalone validator that reports on arbitrary files, including the 9.6 conformance-checking rework

aspose.note: Document.Validate(log, PdfFormat) on any document writes an XML log of problems. PDF/A-1b to PDF/A-4 conversion and validation were improved in 26.8

syncfusion.note: Only reads the declared Conformance level; 2021 validation feature request still undelivered

pdfsharp.note: Docs: 'PDFsharp cannot check whether an existing file is PDF/A-conforming'; vendor uses veraPDF

questpdf.note: Docs send users to external veraPDF; built-in veraPDF validation is only a Future roadmap item.

pdfpig.note: No validator; features cover reading, extraction and basic creation only.

ironpdf.note: No validation API in PdfDocument; the vendor's PDF/A tutorial says to validate with veraPDF or Acrobat Preflight

chromium.note: Generator only; cannot open or validate existing PDFs

itext.note: PDF/UA-1 and PDF/UA-2, with automated conformance checks at creation (UA-1 since 8.0.4, UA-2 since 9.2). WellTaggedPdfDocument (WTPDF) and color-contrast checks were added in 9.6

aspose.note: PDF/UA-1 only: tagged-PDF API, auto-tagging, and validation with PdfFormat.PDF_UA_1. PdfFormat has no PDF/UA-2 member

syncfusion.note: Tagged PDF stated PDF/UA-1 compliant, plus PDF/UA-2 and WTPDF; auto-tagging (alt text still manual)

pdfsharp.note: PDF/UA-1 via UAManager and StructureBuilder, tagging by hand around XGraphics drawing

questpdf.note: PDF/UA-1 via semantic tagging, with automatic table tagging; PDF/UA-2 is on the roadmap.

pdfpig.note: No tagging API; the A-level PDF/A option writes an empty structure tree plus MarkInfo.

ironpdf.note: PDF/UA-1 and PDF/UA-2 (2025.12.2); SaveAsPdfUA tags existing PDFs, RenderHtmlAsPdfUA recommended for full tagging

chromium.note: Tagged PDF (Chrome 85+, Tagged/generateTaggedPDF option); no PDF/UA conformance claim; tags depend on the HTML

itext.note: Core gives PDF/A-3 with associated files, but the developer must embed factur-x.xml and add the ZUGFeRD XMP schema by hand, as the vendor article shows. There is no current dedicated add-on: the old pdfInvoice add-on covered ZUGFeRD 1.0 and was last released in 2018, for iText 7.1

aspose.note: Built in: attach factur-x.xml via FileSpecification with AFRelationship.Alternative, then convert with PdfFormat.ZUGFeRD to PDF/A-3B. You supply the invoice XML yourself

syncfusion.note: ZUGFeRD 1.0, 2.0 and Factur-X profiles (to EN16931, XRechnung) on PDF/A-3b; caller supplies the XML

pdfsharp.note: PsX Factur-X (separate license, delivered as source): Factur-X/ZUGFeRD e-invoices

questpdf.note: Generate PDF/A-3b, then AddAttachment (XML) and ExtendMetadata (XMP); caller supplies both. Docs: ZUGFeRD 2.1.

pdfpig.note: Embedded files are read-only; the writer cannot attach files, so no Factur-X despite PDF/A-3b output.

ironpdf.note: Since v2024.10: caller's XML embedded in PDF/A-3 with ZUGFeRD/Factur-X XMP via EmbedFileConfiguration

chromium.note: Page.printToPDF has no PDF/A-3, file attachment or XMP option

itext.note: The pdfSweep add-on (AGPL or commercial) removes the underlying text, image and vector content in a region. Regex-based cleanup is also available (RegexBasedCleanupStrategy)

aspose.note: RedactionAnnotation.Redact() flattens the annotation and removes the text and images under it; HiddenDataSanitizer (25.11) removes hidden data

syncfusion.note: True removal of text and graphics; existing PDFs on .NET Core need Syncfusion.Pdf.Imaging.Net.Core (same license)

pdfsharp.note: FAQ: no content-manipulation API beyond low-level CLexer; 7.0 preview only adds a Redact annotation type

questpdf.note: The full DocumentOperation list has no redaction, and the product cannot inspect page content.

pdfpig.note: PdfTextRemover strips text for OCR preprocessing; its docs say it 'should not be used to redact content'.

ironpdf.note: RedactTextOnAllPages removes matched text; RedactRegions* black out rectangles (image/path removal not detailed)

chromium.note: Cannot open or modify existing PDFs

capabilities.name: OCR of scanned pages

itext.note: The pdfOCR add-on (AGPL or commercial) runs Tesseract 4 (itext.pdfocr.tesseract4: a library that targets net461 only, or an external executable) or ONNX models (PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, docTR) on ONNX Runtime. Output is PDF or PDF/A-3u

aspose.note: OcrTextAbsorber (Aspose.Pdf.Ocr, since 26.6) returns recognized plain text. Since 26.7 it needs the separately installed Aspose.OCR NuGet package, which is based on ONNX Runtime. Alternatively, Document.Convert(CallBackGetHocr) adds hOCR text from an OCR engine you supply

syncfusion.note: Syncfusion.PDF.OCR.Net.Core: Tesseract and Leptonica native binaries, same Document SDK license

pdfsharp.note: Not in the feature list or the PsX add-ons; the library cannot render pages

questpdf.note: No OCR anywhere; reading content of existing PDFs is not supported at all.

pdfpig.note: No OCR engine; it only exports existing text to hOCR, ALTO or PageXML.

ironpdf.note: PdfDocument.PerformOcr() requires the separately licensed IronOcr package

chromium.note: No PDF input and no OCR component

capabilities.oursNote: M22 writes the text layer from any engine's output; the engine itself is the caller's (ADR 42).

itext.note: The pdfRender add-on is commercial only. There is no native C# version: from .NET it is called as a CLI executable in an external process

aspose.note: PngDevice, JpegDevice, TiffDevice, BmpDevice, GifDevice and EmfDevice; SVG via SvgSaveOptions

syncfusion.note: Syncfusion.PdfToImageConverter.Net.Core: native PDFium plus SkiaSharp, same license

pdfsharp.note: FAQ: 'cannot render PDF files'; the vendor points to GhostScript for page images

questpdf.note: Renders its own documents to PNG, JPEG or WEBP (and SVG) at a set DPI; cannot render existing PDFs.

pdfpig.note: Core cannot render; PdfPig.Rendering.Skia is a separate package by co-maintainer BobLd, using native SkiaSharp.

ironpdf.note: RasterizeToImageFiles and ToBitmap/PageToBitmap

chromium.note: Screenshots render web pages, not PDF pages; headless mode cannot navigate to a PDF document

itext.note: itext.barcodes ships in the core package: Code 128, EAN/UPC, Code 39, Codabar, Interleaved 2 of 5, MSI, POSTNET, PDF417, DataMatrix and QR (the QR encoder is based on zxing code)

aspose.note: Built in only as BarcodeField.AddBarcode, which draws a Code 128 barcode into a barcode form field and makes it read-only. For other symbologies (QR and the like), the vendor uses the separately licensed Aspose.BarCode to generate an image and insert it

syncfusion.note: Built in: Code 11/32/39/93/128, Codabar, EAN-8/13, UPC, QR, Data Matrix, PDF417

pdfsharp.note: PdfSharp.BarCodes ships in the package: Code 3 of 9, Interleaved 2 of 5, OMR; DataMatrix is a stub; no QR

questpdf.note: Not built in: docs show drawing SVG from third-party ZXing.Net, installed separately.

pdfpig.note: No barcode or QR generation; creation covers text, paths, images and links only.

ironpdf.note: Built-in BarcodeStamper for QR Code, Code128 and Code39; other symbologies need the separate IronBarcode

chromium.note: No barcode feature; only via third-party JS/SVG placed in the HTML
